To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Cd concentration of the barrier layer must be in the range of ~35–44% to obtain a type-II Zn1-xCdxTe/Zn0.7-yCdySe/Zn0.3CdySe/ZnP QD structure suitable for the intermediate band solar cell.

to obtain a suitable material system for IBSCs with the intermediate band energy of 0.5–0.7 eV the Zn1−xCdxCdTe/Zn1yCdySe QD material should be grown on the Inp substrate with the Cd concentration in barriers of 35–40% and the QD thickness of 3–4 nm.

(1) the optimal Cd concentration in the barrier layer for the ZnCdTe/ZCdSe QDs is 35–44%; (2) QDs with 0–70% Cd concentration can be used, but the QD thickness is limited to 3–5 nm to achieve the intermediate energy level in the range 0.50 to 0.73 ev; and (3) the barrier thickness has little impact on the results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
determining the optimal parameters for Zn1−xCdxCdTe/Zn1-yCdySe QDs grown on the In1−xGaxP substrate to achieve a high efficiency IBSC.
the design of the QD structure that can be used in IBSCs.
the theoretical determination of the material parameters for type-II ZnCdTe/ZCdSe quantum dot intermediate band solar cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QDs should be thick and have a high Cd content, while the barriers should be thin with high Cd content.

the Zn1−xCdxCdxTe/ZnxZn1−x−ycdCdySe/Zn1−ycdCd1−y quantum dots grown on the Inp substrate are a promising material for IBSCs, provided that their Cd concentration is in the range of Cd concentration in barrier, and the barrier thickness is not less than 2 nm.

to achieve the optimal material parameters for Zn1−xCdxCdTe/Zn1–yCdySe QD IBSCs the QD thickness should be in the range of ∼2.2–3.0 nm, and the Cd concentration in barriers should be in the vicinity of ∼40%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal parameters for ZnCdTe/CdZnSe QDs for an IBSC are a barrier height of ∼0.7 eV and QD height in the range of ∼2–3 eV.
for a given barrier thickness, the QDs with a Cd concentration in the barrier of 40% and in the disk of 60% provide the optimal conditions for IBSCs.
to achieve a desired energy gap of the intermediate band, the thickness of ZnCdSe barrier layer should be at least twice as large as that of QD layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QDs can be grown in a wide variety of sizes and compositions and the optimal material parameters can be found for a specific device structure.
the IBSCs based on ZnCdTe/ZCdSe QDs can be realized on InP substrate with a reasonable efficiency, if the QDs are thick enough.
the IBSCs based on type-II ZnCdTe/ZCdSe QDs can be designed with a high efficiency.
